title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
author: Mark Haddon
current_text: The Wilson County School Board in Tennessee voted to remove The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time from the school system’s approved reading list over its use of the F-bomb, then overturned the ban. The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time was removed from the Lake Fenton, Mich. summer reading program in 2010 after parents complained about its “foul language.” After complaints to the school board about “foul language,” “profane use of God’s name,” and a “negative portrayal of a character with autism or a similar disorder,” a curriculum committee recommended that The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time not be included on the Westmont (PA) Hilltop School District’s voluntary summer reading list. Acting on a parent’s complaints, Olentangy Ohio District Superintendent Scott Davis removed The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time from Liberty High School’s optional summer reading list.

sources.quote: Just a few days ago, the Wilson County School Board in Tennessee voted 3-1 to removed Mark Haddon’s The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time from the school system’s approved reading list over the use of the F-bomb. Just this afternoon, CBLDF learned that the school board has overturned the ban.
